summary: High-level discovery to map regulatory boundaries and operations runbook needs for Cascade Trust. Primary concerns: EEA-only data residency, PHI/HIPAA applicability for certain product flows, audit log retention/serialization, and the need for an operations/incident runbook that outlines access, key management, and breach notification. Redwood AE+SE walked through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs; customer is leaning towards Dedicated or Private given audit constraints but wants to validate latency and cost. Next steps: share compliance artifacts, runbench in EEA, align on fields and retention windows, and draft runbook skeleton.
topics: Audit logging: retention, redaction, export paths
Private deployment / VPC option and KMS integration
Benchmarks: latency vs cost for Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57m
Attendees: Samantha Holt (Redwood AE), Ravi Mendez (Redwood SE), Eliot Park (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (Cascade Head of Security), Priya Nair (Compliance), Miguel Alvarez (Platform), Tom Ellis (CTO), Jamal Reed (PM)

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — I'm Sam Holt, AE on this account. Ravi's our SE and he'll take you through the tech constraints. Eliot's here for ops and handoff. Laura, want to start?
[00:08] Laura: Sure, hi. Thanks. High level: Cascade Trust is evaluating options for model inference for our regulatory reporting assistant. Main ask — we need EEA-only processing for european client data, strong audit trail and ability to prove no unredacted PHI leaves our control.
[00:18] Miguel: We're curious about log exports to Splunk and how retention windows are controlled. Also curious about private networking — can we lock egress?
[00:25] Ravi: Great — we'll cover those. Quick note: we usually see these fall into two patterns: Hosted with region controls vs Dedicated/Private deployments. Each has different operational trade-offs.
[00:34] Jamal: Timeline — Q2 pilot, production in Q3 if everything lines up. Budget is still TBD but we need a compliance signoff path.
[00:40] Samantha: Ok. We'll map controls to your acceptance criteria. Quick question: are you treating this as PHI under HIPAA or more like sensitive financial PII? Priya?
[00:47] Priya: Some flows will include PHI, yes — physician notes in a subset of regulatory reporting. So we need HIPAA controls as well as GDPR DSAR handling. Not every request is PHI but enough that we can't ignore it.
[00:58] Ravi: Understood. Two immediate constraints then: 1) processing location guarantees for EEA, and 2) assurances around PHI — encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and audit logs with exportable retention policies.
[01:10] Tom: Also, our internal security wants an ops runbook: how to respond to a suspected data leak, who has access to key material, proof of key rotation and access logs. We need that documented for our auditors.
[01:20] Samantha: That aligns with a Dedicated or Private deployment conversation. Hosted can do region-level routing for EEA but has shared control plane which some of our enterprise customers can't accept for PHI. We can do Dedicated capacity with isolated GPU pools and bring-your-own KMS for stricter control, or Private for full control plane isolation.
[01:35] Laura: What's the difference operationally for auditability?
[01:38] Ravi: Dedicated gives you tenant-isolated infra with dedicated GPUs — logs and telemetry are exportable, and we support customer-managed KMS in most cases. Private gives you the control plane too; you run the control plane in a VPC and we package the management tools. So Private reduces the 'shared control plane' risk auditors flag. But Private is more ops-heavy on the customer side.
[01:55] Miguel: For Dedicated, will logs ever leave the EEA? Our policy says logs that contain user prompt or model outputs must not be exported outside EEA unless redacted.
[02:03] Ravi: We can configure logging so that the raw transcripts are stored in EEA buckets and exported only to destinations you authorize. We support syslog/Splunk forwarders that can be run into an EEA-only endpoint. There is nuance though: certain metrics/health telemetry can be routed to our central observability unless you opt out.
[02:22] Laura: We need explicit guarantees on telemetry mapping — what's considered telemetry vs data — since sometimes prompt size or example errors are considered sensitive.
[02:28] Samantha: We'll include a telemetry mapping table in the artifacts we share; that was one of the things we planned to send in the attestation bundle.
[02:35] Priya: What's your DPA look like for subprocessors? Who's on your chain?
[02:39] Samantha: Our DPA lists primary subprocessors — cloud provider (we use multi-cloud partners), infra partners for dedicated hardware, and observability providers. We'll share the current DPA and a redlineable template.
[02:46] Tom: On the KMS side — can we use our HSM? We have an HSM appliance tied to our key policies.
[02:51] Ravi: We support customer-managed KMS via standard providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For HSM appliances on-prem you would be looking at Private deployment where you can host the control plane inside your VPC and connect to your HSM via private networking. There's integration work there but it's possible.
[03:08] Jamal: How does deletion requests work? Our DSAR process requires us to delete user content and any derived embeddings within 30 days.
[03:13] Eliot: On retention and deletion — Redwood supports configurable retention windows per route/model. For Hosted we can do soft-delete for X days and purge; Dedicated/Private gives you direct control of the store so you can run filesystem-level purges. Note: embeddings/caches might persist in KV caches until you flush them; that is an operational step.
[03:33] Laura: So flushing KV cache — is that manual or automated? We need to show auditors that when a DSAR comes in we can fully remove associated vectors.
[03:39] Ravi: We have APIs to flush prefix/k-v caches by key and to scrub embedding stores. For Dedicated and Private we can also run background jobs that track references. We'll provide the API docs and an example runbook script for purge.
[03:54] Priya: Are there certifications for the platform? SOC 2 Type II? ISO? Pen test reports?
[03:58] Samantha: Yes — SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation for our hosted control plane; Dedicated customers can request a copy of the SOC reports and we can provide pen test summaries under NDA. We'll send the cert bundle.
[04:09] Miguel: We need to see evidence of regular access reviews and RBAC controls for operator accounts. Our auditors ask for a 90-day access review cadence.
[04:16] Ravi: We support SSO (SAML/OAuth), RBAC with granular roles, and audit logs of operator activity. For Private you'll be running your identity provider integration directly. We'll include the RBAC matrix in the artifacts pack.
[04:28] Jamal: On the risk side — if we do Hosted region EEA-only, what are the failure modes that might move data out? Is there auto-failover to other regions?
[04:36] Samantha: By default Hosted will route to the region you pick and won't fail over to a different region unless a routing policy specifies it. For enterprise customers we can lock policies to avoid cross-region failover. However, in a full region outage you could see degraded service; Dedicated can provide burst or multi-region Dedicated pools but that gets into more architecture.
[04:52] Priya: Also need to understand legal hold. If a subpoena or legal hold arrives, we need a path to freeze and export relevant logs under chain-of-custody.
[04:59] Ravi: We can support forensic exports and chain-of-custody packaging for Dedicated/Private. That includes timestamped audit logs, key access logs, and user activity. For Hosted there is an operational step — we can produce exports but some metadata may be co-located with managed services. We'll detail the differences in the runbook.
[05:14] Tom: Architecturally — curious about model variants and fallback: If you pin a model version in EEA and it's temporarily unhealthy, will your fallback route to a variant in another region?
[05:22] Ravi: Good callout. We have routing policies — by default you can restrict fallbacks to models in the same region and same compliance profile. For emergency fallbacks you can configure a policy, but for you we'd recommend disabling cross-region fallbacks.
[05:33] Miguel: For our pilot we want to validate latency. Can you run a baseline with ~200ms SLA? Our internal SLO is 200-300ms p95 for chat, lower for non-interactive.
[05:42] Ravi: We'll run a latency baseline in the EEA region against a conservative model and share p50/p95/p99. Dedicated will be lower latency due to reserved GPU warm pools and persistent KV caches. We'll note batching tradeoffs for throughput.
[05:55] Priya: Encryption: we need evidence of envelope encryption, key rotation policy, and HSM attestation.
[06:01] Samantha: We'll share our KMS integration docs, rotation frequency, and the mechanism for key access logs. For HSM attestation, Private with your HSM will give you the strongest story; Dedicated with customer-managed KMS also works if you control the keys.
[06:12] Laura: Logging retention — our policy is 7 years for certain audit trails. Is that feasible?
[06:17] Eliot: Seven years is possible but has cost implications. We recommend tiered retention: hot for 90 days, warm for 1-2 years, cold archive for longer-term. We can export to your archive (S3 Glacier EEA). We'll document cost estimates for retention windows.
[06:31] Jamal: Who is the point of contact during incident response? We need an RTO and RACI outlined.
[06:36] Samantha: We'll propose an RACI and SLA matrix. For Dedicated we offer a named support engineer and escalation path. For Private we'd provide runbook templates and onboarding to your on-call rotations.
[06:46] Miguel: SIEM integration — can we stream audit logs to our Splunk in real-time?
[06:50] Ravi: Yes, via secure syslog/TLS endpoints, or via an S3 bucket with notifications. We'll show a Splunk ingestion example. Real-time vs near-real-time depends on your throughput.
[06:59] Priya: A few detailed questions on data subject requests: 1) can you map stored embeddings back to original record IDs; 2) how do you handle model training/updates? Do you ever use customer content to train shared models?
[07:09] Ravi: Embeddings and caches are stored with metadata keys; we can show an export that maps embedding IDs to source IDs. As for training: we do not use customer proprietary data to train our vendor-shared models without explicit consent. You'll have options to opt out of any aggregated telemetry used for model improvement.
[07:24] Laura: Ok, auditors will want documentation. Can you provide a sample runbook for DSAR flow and an example legal hold procedure?
[07:30] Eliot: Yes — that's part of the runbook skeleton we'll send. It will include steps: intake, mapping to keys, flush caches, purge embeddings, export logs, and confirm purge with time-stamped evidence.
[07:40] Jamal: Cost angle — Dedicated has higher baseline cost. Do you have guidance on tradeoffs?
[07:45] Samantha: We provide Optimize tooling to recommend batch sizes, quantization, and caching settings to hit cost targets. We'll run a workload estimate for you. For PHI flows, the compliance cost often pushes to Dedicated/Private but we can show a hybrid: host redacted or pseudonymized traffic in Hosted, sensitive flows in Dedicated.
[07:59] Miguel: Hybrid is interesting. But hybrid increases surface area for audit, gotta be careful.
[08:03] Ravi: Agreed. If you split flows, you'll need strong routing and labeling to ensure sensitive prompts always go to the right endpoint. We support per-route configs and policy tags.
[08:13] Priya: About regional certifications; do you operate EEA datacenters or lease cloud zones?
[08:18] Samantha: We operate in partner cloud regions in EEA (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west). We'll share the region map and exact zones used.
[08:25] Tom: On legal subprocessors — if you use a cloud provider in EEA, are their subprocessors disclosed?
[08:30] Samantha: Yes — that's in the DPA. We'll share the subprocessor list and provide the ability to restrict providers if needed for the contract.
[08:39] Laura: For audits, we sometimes need to run a joint penetration test or receive a SOC2 bridge letter. What are your options?
[08:46] Ravi: We can provide SOC2 reports under NDA and accommodate joint PTs for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can provide pen-test summaries and coordinate on scope. For a full joint PT on our platform we typically go Private.
[08:59] Jamal: Ok, let's talk about the runbook structure you mentioned. Can you outline the high-level sections?
[09:05] Eliot: Sure — suggested runbook skeleton: 1) Roles & contacts, 2) Data classification mapping, 3) DSAR & deletion flows, 4) Incident response and legal hold, 5) KMS key lifecycle & access, 6) Audit evidence generation, 7) Forensics export steps, 8) Escalation matrix. We'll populate this and give you an editable doc.
[09:22] Priya: For DSAR, do you provide a one-click evidence package?
[09:26] Ravi: Not exactly one-click but we have scripted workflows that produce a time-stamped archive containing relevant logs, embeddings mapping, and purge confirmation. We'll provide the script samples.
[09:36] Laura: Redaction — can we redact sensitive tokens automatically before writing to logs?
[09:40] Ravi: Yes, there is a pre-processing hook where you can apply regex or tokenizer-based redaction. We also support on-the-fly pseudonymization and tokenization pipelines. We'll include examples.
[09:53] Tom: Any gotchas with model determinism and KV cache? We need to ensure reproducibility for audits.
[09:57] Ravi: Reproducibility comes down to model versioning and fixed seeds; KV cache is ephemeral and for performance — we can log cache touches and provide ways to snapshot contexts. For audits you would want to log inputs, model version, parameters, and outputs (subject to your retention policy).
[10:13] Jamal: Do you have an SLA for log exports and forensic package delivery?
[10:17] Samantha: For enterprise contracts we can add contractual SLAs for evidence delivery, typically 48-72 hours for forensic packages, faster for urgent requests. We'll scope exact RTO/RPO in the contract.
[10:28] Miguel: We've been using Splunk and have strict network egress policies. Can you support private peering or VPC peering to push logs?
[10:34] Ravi: Yes — Dedicated/Private supports VPC peering and private links. Hosted supports customer-managed endpoints in EEA. We'll provide network diagrams.
[10:44] Priya: A final compliance question: do you support Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA) support or template?
[10:49] Samantha: We can provide DPIA guidance and templates tailored to Redwood usage and include our subprocessors' details. We'll help accelerate your internal DPIA.
[10:57] Laura: Thanks. That covers most of our items. For the pilot we'll probably start with a small Dedicated pool in EEA, run the baseline, and iterate.
[11:05] Samantha: Great — to confirm next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts + DPA draft, Ravi runs baseline in EEA, and we'll produce runbook skeleton + retention cost estimates. Anything else?
[11:15] Tom: Please include cost delta for 1 year retention vs 7 years for logs.
[11:19] Eliot: Noted.
[11:21] Priya: Also include the runbook purge script and example evidence package.
[11:25] Samantha: We'll get those over. Anything else from the group?
[11:28] Jamal: No, thanks.
[11:30] Samantha: We'll follow up with meeting notes and a calendar for a technical baseline run. Appreciate your time.
[57:02] End meeting.

Post-meeting notes (auto): transcription had several overlaps and misheard acronyms (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache, redwood product names occasionally lowercased). Attached artifacts: placeholder links — (Link: SOC2_bundle_redwood.zip), (Link: runbook_skeleton_template.docx), (Link: EEA_latency_baseline_instructions.md).
